device_signature_transcript.note: device_signature is the Ed25519 signature over that signing input under the already registered conformance_ed25519_fixture_key: seed bytes 0x00 through 0x1f, published in the fixtures named above. This fixture therefore carries no private key member of its own, and a verifier can both verify and re-sign. The X25519 HPKE key is the same 32 published seed bytes read as an X25519 scalar, so hpke_key is published test material too and MUST NOT be reused outside conformance fixtures.

verification.note: account_id is injected from the ak.device.authorize Event envelope account actor_id and is not a payload member; device_signature is the output of this transcript and therefore never one of its members.

unit_contract.unit_ordering: wire order, landed as consecutive RealmCommit stream_position in one transaction

mutation_cases.notes: device_authorize_payload is closed and the exact AccountId subject comes from the Event envelope actor_id, so a mirrored principal_id is not a cross-check failure but an invalid payload.
registration_anchor MUST carry 1, the value the same pcr_genesis_unit initializes (device-lifecycle.md section 5.5.2).
authorized_by is a device_id or a did_core_id; under registration_anchor it MUST equal account_id.principal_id and is never a DID.
the transcript without the injected AccountId binds no account.
a bare principal core is not an AccountId; accounts with the same principal at different Stations are permanently distinct.
the signature is the output of this transcript, never one of its members.
section 5.2.1 normalizes a missing optional member to null; an omitted member would be a second canonical byte string for one authorization.
accepted_device signs device_pairing_target_proof under its own domain; a transcript MUST NOT be reused across binding kinds.

constraints: audience and requested_scope are within the handoff ceiling

account_subject_preimage.note: SHA-256 over UTF-8(domain || 0x0A) followed by JCS of the issuer identity and the issuer-local authentication row key. The member names are deployment-local by construction: the subject never leaves the Account Authority boundary, so the specification fixes the domain and the digest but not the row key spelling.

signing_material.note: The identity root is the registration anchor's parameters.updateKeys[0], never a normalized DID document verification method and never the founding device key. The private key is published, so this signature is reproducible and proves no authority.

founding_event_proof_binding.note: The two Events of one genesis unit resolve their signing keys from different material: the create Event from the frozen registration anchor, the authorize Event from the root-signed descriptor and the unit-local candidate overlay. Collapsing both onto one device verification method is what left the registration_anchor admission branch with no constructible instance.

forbidden_verification_method_forms: any fragment resolved through the device directory
a normalized DID document verification method of the principal
the principal actor_id rewritten into a DID URL
any fragment other than the complete device_id
the registration anchor root controller method

provisional_identity_abandonment.credential_rationale: The PCR was never accepted, so the holder has no principal and no principal-bound ak.session.grant can exist.

cases.name: pcr_accepted_before_abandonment_commit
cases.notes: Stable terminal. Removing an established identity is the account deletion path, not provisional-identity abandonment.

cases.name: reserved_identity_creation_is_unreadable_after_abandonment
cases.notes: Security property, not a cleanup policy.

founding_device_key_digest_kat.rule: SHA-256(UTF-8(canonical multikey)); fixed at SHA-256 independently of every domain-selectable Blob or KDF digest suite

device_key_digest.rejected_reason: digesting the whole did:key URI is noncanonical; the receipt binds the bare multikey

hpke_key_digest.transform: none; the canonical multikey exactly as carried

founding_device_key_digest_kat.carrier_rule: the descriptor carries the keys and MUST NOT carry either digest; the receipt carries the digests because it carries no raw key

rules.root_verification_method: did:key:<updateKeys[0]> || '#' || <updateKeys[0]>, the controller proof method of the terminal entry
rules.version_id: '1-' || base58btc(0x12 0x20 || sha256(JCS(terminal entry with versionId replaced by its predecessor and proof omitted)))

signing_material.note: The identity root is the method-native update key and is deliberately not the DID document's published assertion key, which stays the Ed25519 conformance key that crypto-signature-fixture.json resolves under this same DID. This log never publishes a second entry, so nextKeyHashes commits to the same published root key rather than to an unpublished one.

scid_derivation.note: This is the one webvh relation the anchor asserts instead of deriving: every conformance did:webvh SCID is hand-written so it cannot collide with material a deployment produced, and SCID derivation is exercised by the method fixture named above. Everything downstream of the SCID in this anchor is derived.

binds.note: The create Event's initial_resolution carries exactly the did, version_id and method_history_head derived here, and its producer proof verification method is root_verification_method. Replacing the anchor changes anchor_canonical_json_sha256 and therefore invalidates the identity-root control proof that commits to it.

forbidden_substitutions: a resolver summary, a current DID document or a partial log range in place of log_entries
the versionId entry hash in place of the complete anchor digest
a normalized_did_document verification method in place of parameters.updateKeys[0]
the founding device DID URL as the create Event's verification method
a caller-asserted method_history_head that the terminal entry does not hash to

derived_relations.why: The identity-root control proof commits to the whole anchor by this digest, so the digest must be over the complete anchor and not over the versionId entry hash.
method_history_head is the digest of the published terminal entry, proof included; a caller-asserted head is exactly the substitution the branch forbids.
control_key_digest is over the method-native update key multibase, never over a normalized DID document verification method.
The prerotation commitment is the multihash of the next update key; this log publishes one entry, so it commits to the same root key and the commitment stays recomputable.
The inception versionId is the entry hash over the entry with versionId replaced by the SCID and the proof omitted; the whole adapter re-execution turns on it.
The terminal entry's controller proof must actually verify under the update key, over the same entry-hash bytes the versionId commits to.
The derivation summary MUST read back the entry's own versionId rather than restate a constant beside it.
The signed bytes MUST be JCS of the signature-omitted object; without this the transcript could sign one shape and publish another.
And the transcript digest is over that same object.
The identity-root control proof must verify under the anchor's update key, over the domain-prefixed canonical bytes.
The key the control proof verifies under MUST be the anchor's active update key, not a second published key that happens to be Ed25519.
account_subject is the domain-separated digest of the issuer identity and the issuer-local authentication row key, so the deployment-local member names are still bound.
The signed registration_anchor_digest is the anchor digest recomputed above; substituting the anchor therefore invalidates this signature.
So is the signed control_key_digest.
And the signed did_version_id is the entry's own versionId.
And the signed DID is the anchor's DID.
The signed founding_authorize_payload_digest is the digest the root-signed descriptor already carries.
The signed initial_session_request_digest is over the request object itself, so the session the genesis opens is bound rather than described.
Same for the session request's own canonical bytes.
And for the account_subject preimage bytes, so the digest above is over bytes the fixture proves canonical.
